result.topic_en: An algebraic calculation that chooses coefficients so that the cubic $1+\frac{3QQ}{pq}x+\frac{3PQ}{pq}x^2+\frac{Q}{P}x^3$ factors as $(1+\frac{q}{p}x)(1+ax)^2$, then eliminates $a$ and $Q$ to obtain a polynomial relation in $P,p,q$; there is also a small line diagram.
result.transcription:
$\frac{1+ax^2}{ax+x^3}$ [?] \quad $\frac{1+\frac{3PQ}{pq}x^2}{\frac{3PQ}{pq}x+x^3}$
$1+\frac{3QQ}{pq}x+\frac{3PQ}{pq}[-xx-]+\frac{Q}{P}x^3 = (1+\frac{q}{p}x)(1+ax)^2$
$\frac{3QQ}{pq} = \frac{q}{p}+2a$
$\frac{3PQ}{pq} = \frac{2aq}{p}+aa$
$\frac{Q}{P} = \frac{q}{p}aa$
$\frac{3QQ}{pq} = \frac{q}{p}+\frac{2\sqrt{PQpq}}{qP}$
$\frac{3PQ}{pq} = \frac{2\sqrt{PQpq}}{pP}+\frac{pQ}{qP}$
$2\sqrt{PQpq} = \frac{3PQQ-qqP}{p} = \frac{3PPQ-ppQ}{q}$
